PullRequest.Title: Agents - add hover to the repository pickers
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render or refresh the new-session repository configuration toolbar for Agent Host or Copilot sessions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: MenuWorkbenchToolBar synchronously reads visible menu groups, creates the visible picker action view items plus one separator between groups, and renders them before the toolbar is ready. The diff adds only O(A) short group-key formatting and A-1 lightweight separator actions/DOM items; no asynchronous operation is placed on this path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: A is the effective count of repository controls visible for the current scoped session after context-key filtering, not all registrations across sessions. The schema-backed Agent Host path can register V×P global menu entries for V visible sessions and P renderable properties, but the toolbar renders only the current session's P entries; typical built-in configurations expose a small handful.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All grouping, sorting, action creation, and DOM rendering is synchronous on the UI thread. Menu changes remain debounced by the existing menu service; the diff does not add parallel work or a new event source.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Menu/action visibility continues to use existing MenuWorkbenchToolBar and menu-service state. The new group helper has no cache and performs one bounded string conversion per registration/refresh; there is no cold-versus-warm boundary behavior to change.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the added synchronous DOM/allocation work because getActionBarActions inserts a Separator for each additional primary group and ActionViewItem renders one anchor. High confidence that effective visible cardinality is session-filtered and that no boundary call is introduced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Third-party or future provider schemas could expose more properties, but the incremental cost remains one tiny separator item and one short group string per visible property. There is no evidence of realistically large cardinality or frame-frequency rebuilds sufficient for a reportable regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The extra synchronous work is linear in the already-rendered, realistically small action count and is the intentional mechanism for visual separators.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, filter, and close an Agent Host repository branch/configuration picker
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For a dynamic enum, the existing provider.getSessionConfigCompletions call must finish before the action widget can open; static and boolean pickers stay local. After that existing await, the diff performs one ancestor lookup and two attribute writes on open/close to drive hover/expanded styling.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve dynamic session configuration completions through IAgentConnection.sessionConfigCompletions to the local or remote agent host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request on each dynamic picker open, plus one coalesced request for each settled filter query; static enum and boolean properties issue none.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same completion call, await, item mapping, and filter Delayer were already on the open/filter path; the PR only adds DOM state for branch-picker styling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The request is awaited before the picker is shown, exactly as before the PR. The new closest lookup and attribute writes run only after it completes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One initial completion request per dynamic-picker open, followed by existing delayed completion requests as the user changes a filter query. Attribute and closest work is constant per open/close and does not scale with completion-item count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The initial open awaits one provider request. Filter requests remain scheduled through the existing Delayer, which coalesces rapid input; the diff changes neither request concurrency nor ordering.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Dynamic value labels continue to be cached per session/property, while completion results themselves are requested as before. The new picker-open DOM state has no retained cache and is removed by the existing onHide lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from tracing _showPicker through _getItems to provider.getSessionConfigCompletions and IAgentConnection.sessionConfigCompletions, and from the changed lines being after the existing await.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote completion latency varies, but it is pre-existing and its frequency, payload, scheduling, and critical-path placement are unchanged. The added DOM operations are constant-time over a shallow toolbar subtree.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The only expensive boundary is pre-existing; the diff adds bounded DOM work once per user open/close.

Scenarios.Scenario: Refresh repository menu registrations when visible sessions, provider configuration, or phone layout changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing contribution synchronously clears registrations, iterates visible sessions and renderable schema properties, and re-registers menu items; menu listeners then rebuild affected toolbars. The diff replaces each constant group name with a stable padded group string, without adding a new refresh trigger or additional provider lookup.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Work remains O(V×P) for V visible sessions and P renderable properties during a refresh. The changed portion adds one bounded string construction per existing menu item; visible toolbars still context-filter to one session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Refreshes remain synchronous event/autorun work. Provider listeners, context-key listeners, and visible-session autorun are unchanged; no new concurrency, queue, or burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Command/action-view registrations remain retained in the existing DisposableMap and menu items in the existing DisposableStore, which is cleared each refresh. Group strings live only with their corresponding existing menu registrations and are disposed on the same lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from constructor listener tracing and _refreshRepositoryMenuItems: all refresh sources and provider/config reads predate the diff, and the only changed operation inside the loop is group-key formatting.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The maximum number of visible sessions and provider-defined properties is not fixed here, but the PR neither changes that cardinality nor adds collection-wide work beyond a short string format for each already-created registration.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Existing O(V×P) refresh behavior is not materially amplified by the bounded string allocation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Hover repository controls and keep the repository action bar highlighted while its branch picker is open
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Pointer hover and picker open/close trigger normal selector matching and repaint for the small toolbar container. The changed CSS uses background/color state and does not add geometry reads, filters, animations, transitions, or nested synchronous relayout.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost is bounded by the repository toolbar's small visible action count and user hover/open events; it does not scale with chat history, repository size, branch count, or frame-driven animation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Browser style and paint work is event-driven with no JavaScript loop or asynchronous fan-out. Attribute writes happen once on open and once on hide.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache is involved. CSS matching and browser style caches are used normally; the data-picker-open attribute is removed on hide, so no state accumulates across picker lifetimes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the changed selectors/declarations and picker lifecycle: the diff adds only bounded style state and no layout read-after-write path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact paint cost varies by theme/compositor, but the affected area is a small control bar and the declarations are simple colors/background images without known high-cost effects.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The rendering work is small, user-driven, and bounded.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 13 changed files and every diff page. Traced toolbar construction, separator rendering, repository menu refreshes, picker lifecycle, dynamic completion IPC/network calls, style/paint behavior, effective cardinality, caching, and concurrency. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression or concrete regression fix was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
